# Robinhood Wallet Connector

> **AI agents: start with [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt).** [Raw text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Full documentation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms-full.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

**Connect Robinhood Wallet to mainstream frontend wallet SDKs.**

An open-source integration toolkit for dApp developers, with adapters for **wagmi v2/v3, RainbowKit, and Web3-Onboard**, plus a framework-independent **EIP-1193 provider**. Use it to add a recognizable Robinhood Wallet entry and a dedicated connection dialog to your application.

Built and maintained by **[Vexi Lab](https://vexi-protocol.ai) (an onchain options protocol)**. This is an independent community project, **not an official Robinhood SDK**, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Robinhood.

A matching injected Robinhood provider is used when available; otherwise, the SDK offers a QR code and an explicit **Open Robinhood Wallet** action through WalletConnect. Each integration includes usage documentation and a runnable example below.

## Packages

| Package | Purpose | Integration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@vexi/robinhood-wallet` | Framework-independent EIP-1193 provider and connection UI | [Core API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/core/README.md) |
| `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi` | wagmi connector | [Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/wagmi/README.md) · [v2 example](https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/tree/main/examples/wagmi-v2) · [v3 example](https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/tree/main/examples/wagmi-v3) |
| `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-rainbowkit` | Robinhood entry for `connectorsForWallets` | [Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/rainbowkit/README.md) · [Example](https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/tree/main/examples/rainbowkit) |
| `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-onboard` | Standard Web3-Onboard wallet module | [Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/web3-onboard/README.md) · [Example](https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/tree/main/examples/onboard) |

The core owns its connection lifecycle and native HTML dialog. It uses `@walletconnect/sign-client` directly and does not depend on AppKit modal internals or patches to a framework wallet chooser. Construction and imports do not request accounts or launch a wallet.

## Install from this repository

These packages have **not been published to npm**. Build and pack the repository, then install the generated tarballs in your application. Node.js 22.12 or newer is required for this development workflow.

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
mkdir -p artifacts
npm pack --workspaces --pack-destination artifacts
```

For a standalone provider, install the core tarball:

```sh
npm install /path/to/artifacts/vexi-robinhood-wallet-0.1.0.tgz
```

Install all required local SDK packages in the **same install command**, so npm can resolve their unpublished dependencies:

| Integration | Required tarballs |
| --- | --- |
| wagmi | `vexi-robinhood-wallet-0.1.0.tgz`, `vexi-robinhood-wallet-wagmi-0.1.0.tgz` |
| RainbowKit | Core and wagmi tarballs above, plus `vexi-robinhood-wallet-rainbowkit-0.1.0.tgz` |
| Web3-Onboard | Core tarball, plus `vexi-robinhood-wallet-onboard-0.1.0.tgz` |

For example, in an existing wagmi v2 application:

```sh
npm install \
  /path/to/artifacts/vexi-robinhood-wallet-0.1.0.tgz \
  /path/to/artifacts/vexi-robinhood-wallet-wagmi-0.1.0.tgz \
  wagmi@2.19.5 @wagmi/core@2.22.1 viem@2.57.7
```

Use your own WalletConnect project ID and allow the application origin in its project settings. The project ID is browser configuration; the SDK never needs a private key or recovery phrase.

## Use with wagmi

```ts
import { createConfig, http } from 'wagmi';
import { mainnet } from 'wagmi/chains';
import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi';

export const config = createConfig({
  chains: [mainnet],
  connectors: [robinhoodWallet({
    projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID',
    metadata: {
      name: 'My app',
      description: 'My app description',
      url: 'https://my-app.example',
      icons: [],
    },
  })],
  transports: { [mainnet.id]: http() },
});
```

Use the resulting connector with wagmi's normal connection hooks or actions. A user selecting **Connect** starts the permission request. The adapter exposes `cancelConnect()` for custom host controls. The runnable examples include the React provider setup.

As with wagmi's built-in connectors, a `chainId` passed to `connect` is a preference: if switching to it fails, the connection stays on the wallet's chain, and only a user rejection fails it. A previously approved session is recovered on reconnect, and by `connect` itself, without a new approval.

## Use with RainbowKit

```ts
import { connectorsForWallets } from '@rainbow-me/rainbowkit';
import { injectedWallet, walletConnectWallet } from '@rainbow-me/rainbowkit/wallets';
import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-rainbowkit';

const connectors = connectorsForWallets([
  { groupName: 'Recommended', wallets: [robinhoodWallet] },
  { groupName: 'Other wallets', wallets: [injectedWallet, walletConnectWallet] },
], {
  projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID',
  appName: 'My app',
  appUrl: 'https://my-app.example',
});
```

Pass `connectors` to wagmi's `createConfig`. Selecting Robinhood opens the SDK's native modal above the RainbowKit chooser. The underlying page becomes inert while the modal is open; Close or Escape cancels the SDK attempt. After an error, close the dialog and select Robinhood again to start a fresh request. Other wallets remain ordinary RainbowKit entries.

The adapter consumes application metadata from `walletConnectParameters.metadata`; other generic WalletConnect options are not forwarded. RainbowKit can reorder installed and recent wallets according to its own settings.

## Use with Web3-Onboard

```ts
import Onboard from '@web3-onboard/core';
import { robinhoodModule } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-onboard';

const onboard = Onboard({
  wallets: [robinhoodModule({ projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID' })],
  chains: [{
    id: '0x1',
    token: 'ETH',
    label: 'Ethereum',
    rpcUrl: 'https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com',
  }],
  appMetadata: { name: 'My app', description: 'My app description', explore: 'https://my-app.example' },
});

// Call from your Connect button's handler.
async function connectWallet() {
  await onboard.connectWallet();
}
```

Onboard supplies the configured chains, RPC endpoints, and application metadata to the module. Its interface exposes the EIP-1193 provider and the same `RobinhoodProvider` as `instance`. When Onboard reconnects through `eth_requestAccounts`, the provider recovers the previously approved session instead of starting a new pairing.

The tested Onboard dependency tree includes inherited critical and high-severity registry advisories. Review the [dependency notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/dependency-notes.md) before adopting this integration; a passing framework test is not a security certification.

## Framework versions

The manifests intentionally use exact peer versions. The verification record distinguishes completed checks from pending work; these entries are not broad version-range or physical-wallet compatibility claims.

| Integration | Declared baseline |
| --- | --- |
| wagmi v2 | `wagmi 2.19.5`, `@wagmi/core 2.22.1`, `viem 2.57.7` |
| wagmi v3 | `wagmi 3.7.7`, `@wagmi/core 3.6.5`, `viem 2.57.7` |
| RainbowKit | `@rainbow-me/rainbowkit 2.2.11`, wagmi v2 baseline above |
| Web3-Onboard | `@web3-onboard/core 2.24.1`, `@web3-onboard/common 2.4.2` |

RainbowKit's listed baseline uses wagmi v2. The separate wagmi v3 example does not establish RainbowKit compatibility with wagmi v3.

## Connection and verification boundaries

The desktop layout presents a locally generated QR code; narrow viewports use a bottom sheet with the same explicit app-opening action. The SDK does not infer that an app is installed from viewport size. It never signs or sends a transaction automatically. A later application request can ask the connected wallet to approve a supported operation.

The dialog renders inside a shadow root, so the host page's CSS cannot restyle its QR code or controls. In browsers with constructable stylesheets it needs no inline `<style>` element, so it also works under a `style-src 'self'` Content Security Policy; the embedded icon still needs `img-src data:`.

Configured EVM chain IDs are application inputs, not proof of wallet support. Remote sessions must approve the requested chain, account, and method. Robinhood Chain mainnet `4663` and testnet `46630` require separate device and network evidence; neither is certified by this delivery.

Physical Robinhood Wallet pairing, iOS/Android app routing, signatures, and transaction submission remain unverified. Synthetic tests, package builds, and a rendered QR code do not establish those outcomes. See [verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md) for recorded evidence and the device checklist.

```sh
npm run build

```

The matrix packs the packages, installs real framework dependencies in isolated temporary applications, builds the examples, and runs synthetic lifecycle checks. It does not request real wallet approval.

See [architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/architecture.md), [verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md), and [upstream assessment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/upstream-contributions.md). Package publication, upstream inclusion, deployment, and physical-wallet certification are separate delivery stages.

# Robinhood Wallet integration guide for AI coding agents

Use this guide to add Robinhood Wallet to an existing frontend application. This repository provides a standalone EIP-1193 provider and adapters for wagmi v2/v3, RainbowKit and Web3-Onboard.

Built by **[Vexi Lab](https://vexi-protocol.ai) (an onchain options protocol)**. This is an independent community project, not an official Robinhood SDK, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Robinhood.

## Choose an integration

Inspect the application's existing wallet framework and dependency versions before choosing a package. Match the exact [supported framework baselines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#framework-versions); do not infer support for other versions or frameworks from shared dependencies.

| Existing application | Public entry point | Guide and runnable source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| wagmi v2 | `import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi'` | [Adapter guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/wagmi/README.md), [example setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/wagmi-v2/README.md), [React app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/wagmi-v2/src/main.tsx) |
| wagmi v3 | Same wagmi entry point | [Adapter guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/wagmi/README.md), [example setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/wagmi-v3/README.md), [React app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/wagmi-v3/src/main.tsx) |
| RainbowKit with wagmi v2 | `import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-rainbowkit'` | [Adapter guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/rainbowkit/README.md), [example setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/rainbowkit/README.md), [React app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/rainbowkit/src/main.tsx) |
| Web3-Onboard | `import { robinhoodModule } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-onboard'` | [Module guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/web3-onboard/README.md), [example setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/onboard/README.md), [app source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/onboard/src/main.ts) |
| Vanilla browser or a host that accepts an EIP-1193 provider | `import { RobinhoodProvider } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet'` | [Core API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/core/README.md), [example setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/vanilla/README.md), [app source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/vanilla/main.ts) |

The two `robinhoodWallet` exports serve different APIs: call the wagmi factory with options and put its result in `createConfig({ connectors })`; pass the RainbowKit factory without calling it in a `connectorsForWallets` wallet group. Call `robinhoodModule(options)` for `Onboard({ wallets })`. Keep the application's other wallet entries and provider wrappers intact.

This repository does not yet provide tested adapters for Reown AppKit, ConnectKit, thirdweb or Dynamic, or a verified Privy integration. Its EIP-1193 interface is an integration starting point, not evidence of compatibility with those SDKs. RainbowKit uses the documented wagmi v2 baseline; the separate wagmi v3 example does not extend that claim.

## Install the actual packages

The packages are **unpublished**. Do not suggest installing these `@vexi` package names directly from the npm registry. With Node.js 22.12 or newer, prepare tarballs from a checkout:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector.git
cd robinhood-wallet-connector
npm ci
npm run build
mkdir -p artifacts
npm pack --workspaces --pack-destination artifacts
```

In the consuming application, install the required tarballs together in one `npm install` command so npm can resolve their unpublished dependencies:

| Integration | Local SDK packages required |
| --- | --- |
| Core | `@vexi/robinhood-wallet` |
| wagmi | Core + `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi` |
| RainbowKit | Core + wagmi adapter + `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-rainbowkit` |
| Web3-Onboard | Core + `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-onboard` |

Use the exact tarball filenames and installation example in the [installation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository), and install the chosen framework's declared peer dependencies. The examples' `package.json` files provide working dependency sets. The packages expose ESM and TypeScript declarations; use public `import` entry points, not CommonJS `require` or files from `src`, `dist` or the internal modal implementation.

## Configure the host application

1. Supply your own WalletConnect `projectId` and allow the application's actual origin in that project's settings. In the Vite examples, copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`, set `VITE_WC_PROJECT_ID`, and restart the development server. The ID is public application configuration; no wallet private key or recovery phrase belongs here.
2. Provide application metadata with a name, description, absolute HTTP(S) URL and icon array. For RainbowKit, pass `appName` and `appUrl` to `connectorsForWallets`. For Onboard, supply `appMetadata` or explicit module `metadata`.
3. Configure the EVM chain IDs and usable RPC endpoints. Core takes numeric `chains` and `rpcMap`; wagmi derives them from its configured chains with an optional `rpcMap` override; Onboard derives them from its chain entries, which use hexadecimal IDs such as `0x1`. Use the existing application chain setup when appropriate.
4. Create a stable provider or connector configuration rather than creating another instance on every render. If independent core/wagmi/Onboard instances need separate persisted sessions, give them distinct, stable `storagePrefix` values.
5. Start connection only from the user's Connect action, using the framework's normal connection API or `provider.connect()`. Display pending, cancellation and error states; prevent repeated host clicks while pending. Connecting does not automatically sign or send transactions.

Imports and core construction are safe without `window`, but interactive wallet use requires a browser. Supply metadata URLs explicitly for server rendering; the runnable Vite examples use `window.location.origin` and need adaptation before copying into server-executed code. Keep the consuming framework's own client/server boundaries intact.

The default UI requires native `HTMLDialogElement.showModal()` and Shadow DOM. It renders in a shadow root under one `<rhw-connector>` element, so the host page's CSS does not restyle it. Where constructable stylesheets are supported, it needs no inline `<style>` element, so a `style-src 'self'` Content Security Policy works; the embedded icon still needs `img-src data:`. See the [core UI requirements](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/core/README.md#discovery-and-session-scope) if the host needs a custom UI.

## Preserve the connection lifecycle

| Host action or condition | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | Use the chosen adapter or `provider.connect({ chainId })`. A previously approved, persisted session is recovered first, without a new approval. Otherwise a matching Robinhood injected provider is preferred, and failing that the SDK pairs through WalletConnect with its dedicated Robinhood dialog. Core `connect({ chainId })` requires that chain; the wagmi and RainbowKit adapters treat a requested chain as a preference, as wagmi's built-in connectors do, and fail only when the user rejects the switch. |
| Cancel pending connection | Close the SDK dialog or press Escape. Custom controls can call `provider.cancel()` or the wagmi connector's `cancelConnect()`. Core cancellation rejects with code `4001`; wagmi maps it to its normal user-rejection error. A wallet rejection that WalletConnect reports as `USER_REJECTED` also arrives as `4001`. Cancellation does not revoke an established connection, interrupt its requests, or dismiss an injected wallet's own permission prompt. |
| Retry after rejection, cancellation or error | Settle the old host request, close any error dialog, and start a fresh request from a new user action. Do not automatically reopen permission prompts. Core shares matching concurrent attempts; the wagmi adapter shares a repeated pending connect and rejects one for a different chain with `ResourceUnavailableRpcError`. |
| Recover after reload | Use the framework's reconnect flow, `provider.isAuthorized()`, or an explicit Connect. Recovery checks previously approved state without requesting account permission and may initialize remote transport; it keeps the session's approved chain and account selection, and revokes a session that approves none of the configured chains. `eth_accounts` alone only reads the current instance's cache. |
| Account or chain changes | Use the framework's reactive state. With core, subscribe to `accountsChanged`, `chainChanged` and `disconnect`; update application state and remove listeners on disposal. An empty account list means access is gone. |
| Disconnect | Use the framework's disconnect API or `provider.disconnect()`. This clears local state and disconnects this transport's approved remote session and its pairing. Wallet-side revocation is best effort: the promise resolves after local cleanup even when the wallet cannot be reached. It does not revoke injected-wallet permissions. |
| Dispose a core instance | `provider.destroy()` releases its UI and listeners while preserving an approved persisted session for recovery by a later instance. It is not a logout action; the destroyed instance cannot reconnect. |

Core `connect()` returns a numeric `chainId`; EIP-1193 `chainChanged` and `eth_chainId` use hexadecimal strings. Before connection, the core `getChainId()` reflects the configured initial chain, not wallet approval; the wagmi connector's `getChainId()` reports an in-app Robinhood wallet's current chain when one is present, read with `eth_chainId` and no permission request. See the [core API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/core/README.md#api) for complete methods, events and session semantics.

## Avoid common integration mistakes

- **One pairing UI:** leave the SDK's dialog enabled when using the supplied adapters. Do not add a generic WalletConnect/AppKit pairing modal around it. RainbowKit's chooser and the SDK dialog have separate roles; the chooser is inert during SDK pairing.
- **Custom UI is a complete responsibility:** for integrations exposing `showModal: false`, subscribe to `display_uri` before connecting, provide QR/link rendering and cancellation, and clear sensitive pairing data after cancellation or completion. Import `getRobinhoodUri` from the core to construct the app link, and open it only on an explicit click. Follow the [custom UI contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/core/README.md#custom-connection-ui).
- **Wallet identity:** discovery uses `com.robinhood.wallet` EIP-6963 metadata or `isRobinhoodMobileWallet`. Do not rename an arbitrary injected provider or a generic WalletConnect connector to Robinhood. These identity hints are not cryptographic vendor authentication.
- **Network approval:** adding a chain ID does not establish wallet support. A remote session must approve the requested chain, accounts and methods. Switching between chains the session approved is local and shows no wallet prompt; a chain the session did not approve is rejected with `4901`. Robinhood Chain mainnet `4663` and testnet `46630` each need their own device/network evidence.
- **Sensitive data:** keep pairing URIs, session keys and wallet account information out of analytics, logs, screenshots and error reports. A public WalletConnect project ID does not make pairing material public.
- **Dependency risk:** read the [dependency notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/dependency-notes.md), especially for the documented inherited Onboard advisories. Passing integration tests is not a security audit.

## Verify and describe the result

Use the selected example to verify the normal framework flow and run the consuming application's build and type checks. For changes to this repository, follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/CONTRIBUTING.md); the packed-package matrix supports `wagmi-v2`, `wagmi-v3`, `rainbowkit` and `onboard` cases.

Check user-triggered connection, cancellation, retry, pending-state cleanup, disconnect, restored sessions, account/chain events and other wallet entries. UI work also needs desktop/narrow-viewport, keyboard and focus checks. The [vanilla fixture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/vanilla/fixture.ts) offers a synthetic transport for repeatable UI checks; its QR cannot pair a real wallet.

Report the exact framework versions and checks performed. Keep synthetic tests, browser relay checks and physical-wallet results separate. Physical iOS/Android pairing, app routing, signatures and transaction submission remain unverified in the [verification record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md); do not present a rendered QR or a successful build as proof of them. Real wallet approval and signing belong to a separately authorized manual test.

# Source: packages/core/README.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/core/README.md

# Robinhood Wallet provider

> **AI integration docs:** [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

`@vexi/robinhood-wallet` provides a framework-independent EIP-1193 provider and a dedicated Robinhood Wallet connection dialog for frontend applications. It is the shared core behind this toolkit's wagmi, RainbowKit and Web3-Onboard adapters.

Built and maintained by **[Vexi Lab](https://vexi-protocol.ai) (an onchain options protocol)**. This is an independent community project, **not an official Robinhood SDK**, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Robinhood.

This package is currently unpublished. Build the repository and install `vexi-robinhood-wallet-0.1.0.tgz` generated by `npm pack`; see the [repository installation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository). ESM and TypeScript declarations are included. Node.js 22.12 or newer is the development baseline; wallet interaction runs in the browser.

## Minimal browser usage

```ts
import { RobinhoodProvider } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet';

const provider = new RobinhoodProvider({
  projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID',
  chains: [1],
  rpcMap: { 1: 'https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com' },
  metadata: {
    name: 'My app',
    description: 'My app description',
    url: 'https://my-app.example',
    icons: [],
  },
});

// Wire these functions to user controls in your application.
async function connectWallet() {
  try {
    const { accounts, chainId } = await provider.connect({ chainId: 1 });
    return { accounts, chainId };
  } catch {
    // Present a local error or retry control. Do not log pairing material.
    return undefined;
  }
}

async function disconnectWallet() {
  await provider.disconnect();
}
```

Constructing the provider does not request accounts, initialize the remote transport, or open a dialog. Invoke `connect()` or `eth_requestAccounts` only after the user chooses to connect. A real WalletConnect project ID with the application's origin allowed is required for remote pairing.

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `projectId: string` | WalletConnect project ID used when remote transport is needed. |
| `chains: readonly number[]` | Nonempty list of configured EVM chain IDs. The first initializes the local chain value. |
| `optionalChains?: readonly number[]` | Additional configured EVM chain IDs offered to the wallet. |
| `rpcMap?: Record<number, string>` | RPC endpoints used for supported read requests through the remote provider. |
| `metadata` | Application `{ name, description, url, icons }`. Supply an HTTP(S) application URL. |
| `showModal?: boolean` | Defaults to `true`. Set `false` only when the host handles connection links and cancellation. |
| `connectTimeoutMs?: number` | Attempt timeout, default `120000`. |
| `discoveryTimeoutMs?: number` | Injected-provider discovery window, default `200`. |
| `storagePrefix?: string` | Isolates this connector's persisted session state; defaults to a project-ID-based prefix. |

Both chain arrays form the offered remote namespace. They are not a claim that Robinhood supports all entries, and approval of every configured chain is not required. `connect({ chainId })` requires approval of that specific configured chain. Remote operations also require the relevant session permission.

Give distinct independent connector instances distinct stable `storagePrefix` values. Reusing a prefix intentionally shares the persisted session namespace. Keep the prefix stable across reloads when session recovery is desired.

## API

| API | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `connect({ chainId? }?)` | Returns `{ accounts: string[], chainId: number }`. First recovers this connector's previously approved, persisted session without a new approval request. Otherwise opens the remote dialog if no matching injected provider is found. |
| `request({ method, params? })` | EIP-1193 request. `eth_requestAccounts` starts connection, with the same session recovery as `connect()`; `eth_accounts` reads the local cache; `eth_chainId` returns a hexadecimal chain ID. Other requests require a connection. |
| `cancel()` | Cancels a pending attempt, or the session recovery that `connect()` is waiting on, and closes its dialog. Does not disconnect an established connection or interrupt its requests. |
| `disconnect()` | Cancels pending work, clears local account/session selection, and disconnects this transport's approved remote session and its pairing. Injected wallet permissions are not revoked. Wallet-side revocation is best effort: when the wallet cannot be reached, local state is still cleared and the promise resolves. |
| `destroy()` | Releases this provider's UI and listeners. Preserves an approved persisted session for a later provider instance; does not revoke it. The destroyed instance cannot reconnect. |
| `isAuthorized()` | Attempts to recover this connector's previously approved session without requesting account permission. Returns `boolean`; may initialize remote transport to inspect saved state. |
| `getAccounts()` | Returns a copy of the current cached accounts, or an empty list before connection/recovery. |
| `getChainId()` | Returns the local numeric chain ID. Before connection, this is the first configured chain, not a wallet confirmation. |
| `status` | `idle`, `connecting`, or `connected`. |
| `transport` | `injected`, `walletConnect`, or `undefined`. |
| `connected` | Whether this instance has adopted a connection. |
| `on(event, listener)` / `removeListener(event, listener)` | Subscribe to or remove a provider event listener. |

No connection method automatically requests a signature or submits a transaction. The generic `request()` API can forward signing or transaction methods only when an application explicitly requests them and the connected wallet/session supports them. Wallet approval and rejection remain wallet decisions.

### Events

The provider emits `connect` with `{ chainId: string }`, `accountsChanged` with an account array, `chainChanged` with a hexadecimal string, `disconnect`, and forwarded `message` events. Remote pairing emits `display_uri` with sensitive WalletConnect pairing material.

Keep connection state current through events instead of assuming a connection remains valid indefinitely. Remove your listeners when the host component is disposed. A changed chain or empty account list must be handled by the host application.

Events report actual changes: a chain switch or session update that leaves the account list unchanged does not emit `accountsChanged`. When the wallet removes every account, the provider emits one empty `accountsChanged` and then `disconnect`, even if a listener disconnects in between. A listener that throws is reported through the platform `reportError()` where available, as `EventTarget` does, and never interrupts the provider.

### Retry and cancellation

Matching concurrent core connection requests share the current attempt; a conflicting requested chain is rejected. Closing the SDK dialog or pressing Escape rejects the pending attempt with code `4001`. A timeout also terminates the attempt. Late remote approval is cleaned up for its original session topic instead of adopting it after cancellation.

A wallet that rejects the connection proposal or a request with WalletConnect's `USER_REJECTED` codes (`5000`–`5003`) is reported with EIP-1193 code `4001`; the original WalletConnect error is kept as `data`.

The default error view keeps a Close action and explains how to retry from the application. Call `connect()` again from a new host action to create a fresh request. The framework adapters retain their framework's normal error and connection state.

### Custom connection UI

With `showModal: false`, subscribe to `display_uri` before connecting and handle the link in your own UI. Use exported `getRobinhoodUri(uri)` to validate a WalletConnect v2 URI and construct the `robinhood-wallet://wc?uri=...` app link. Launch that link only after an explicit user action.

Your UI must offer cancellation through `provider.cancel()`, clear its QR/link on close and completion, and ignore results from an obsolete attempt. Do not send pairing URIs to QR services, analytics, logs, or error-reporting systems. The default modal generates its QR in the browser and clears the URI and canvas when closed.

`ConnectionModal` and `ProviderDependencies` describe the internal host/test seams. `RobinhoodModal` is an implementation detail, not a public package export.

## Discovery and session scope

Discovery checks the published `com.robinhood.wallet` EIP-6963 identity and the `isRobinhoodMobileWallet` injected-provider flag. It does not select an arbitrary `window.ethereum` provider and change its label. These hints distinguish compatible provider advertisements; they are not cryptographic vendor authentication.

Remote connections use `@walletconnect/sign-client` **2.26.0**. The core owns its approved session topic and requests only within its authorized EVM namespace. Read calls use the corresponding configured `rpcMap` endpoint. The SDK uses browser persistence where available, while WalletConnect maintains its own session/key storage. Providers that share a storage prefix share one SignClient per page, created with the first provider's project ID and metadata, because WalletConnect keeps one Core per prefix; a provider created after `destroy()` reuses it.

A restored session is validated for expiry and approved accounts/chains before adoption. It keeps the saved chain and account selection while the session still approves them; if the saved chain is no longer configured, it uses another configured chain the session approved. A session that approves none of the configured chains is revoked rather than left approved.

Switching between chains the session already approved is local, as in WalletConnect's `UniversalProvider`: every request names its chain, so the wallet is not prompted. A chain the session did not approve is rejected with `4901`. Session events may encode chains as numbers, hexadecimal or decimal strings, or CAIP-2 IDs, and accounts as addresses or CAIP-10 IDs; the decoded values are still checked against the session's approval. A wallet's session extension is honored.

Imports and construction are safe without a browser. Interactive use requires a browser; the default modal requires native `HTMLDialogElement.showModal()` and Shadow DOM. The dialog renders in a shadow root under a single `<rhw-connector>` element, so host page CSS does not restyle it. Where constructable stylesheets are supported, its CSS is applied without an inline `<style>` element, so a `style-src 'self'` Content Security Policy works; other browsers fall back to an inline style element. The icon is an embedded data URL, so the policy must still allow `img-src data:`, or the application should supply its own UI.

## Verification and licensing

Framework builds, synthetic lifecycle tests, real browser checks, and physical-wallet tests are separate evidence. Actual iOS/Android pairing, signatures, transaction submission, and Robinhood Chain `4663`/`46630` support remain unverified. Configuring a chain does not certify it. Consult the repository's [verification record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md) for the current evidence scope.

Code is MIT-licensed. Third-party names and branding are not relicensed under MIT and do not imply endorsement. The embedded Robinhood icon is attributed to the [Robinhood Wallet App Store listing, ID 1634080733](https://apps.apple.com/app/id1634080733); its PNG SHA-256 is `8036938af96b8d0a7fec88c8bdb8e5fbc1ef59e7759b55d5d59667f7513fa951`.

# Source: packages/wagmi/README.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/wagmi/README.md

# Robinhood Wallet for wagmi

> **AI integration docs:** [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

Connect Robinhood Wallet to wagmi v2/v3 using the toolkit's provider and dedicated connection dialog.

Built and maintained by **[Vexi Lab](https://vexi-protocol.ai) (an onchain options protocol)**. This is an independent community project, **not an official Robinhood SDK**, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Robinhood.

These packages are not published to npm. Follow the [tarball installation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository) before using this adapter.

```ts
import { createConfig, http } from 'wagmi';
import { mainnet } from 'wagmi/chains';
import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi';

export const config = createConfig({
  chains: [mainnet],
  connectors: [robinhoodWallet({
    projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID',
    metadata: {
      name: 'My app',
      description: 'My app description',
      url: 'https://my-app.example',
      icons: [],
    },
  })],
  transports: { [mainnet.id]: http() },
});
```

Use wagmi's normal `useConnect`, `useDisconnect`, and wallet client APIs. Connection requests start only after an explicit connect action. A discovered Robinhood provider is selected by its published identity hints; other injected providers are never relabeled. Without one, the SDK opens a dedicated Robinhood dialog using WalletConnect as transport.

`getProvider()` returns the stable `RobinhoodProvider`. `cancelConnect()` cancels only a pending attempt. `disconnect()` clears the connector's session and listeners; it does not revoke permissions in another wallet or modify another connector's session. Chain switching requires a configured chain and actual wallet confirmation. The chain list is application configuration, not evidence that Robinhood supports every configured network.

As with wagmi's built-in `injected` and `walletConnect` connectors, a `chainId` passed to `connect` is a preference. After the wallet approves, the connector asks to switch; if the switch fails, the connection stays on the wallet's chain, and only a user rejection fails it. Before connecting, `getChainId()` reports an in-app Robinhood wallet's current chain (read with `eth_chainId`, which needs no account permission), so hosts such as RainbowKit do not request a needless switch. Without one, it reports the first configured chain. A repeated `connect` while one is pending shares that request; one for a different chain fails with `ResourceUnavailableRpcError`.

Compatibility baselines: wagmi **2.19.5** / `@wagmi/core` **2.22.1**, or wagmi **3.7.7** / `@wagmi/core` **3.6.5**, with Viem **2.57.7**. The repository matrix validates packed packages against both. Runnable examples are in `examples/wagmi-v2` and `examples/wagmi-v3`.

Use `showModal: false` only if your host handles `display_uri` and exposes cancellation. `isAuthorized()` and reconnection never request account permission. SSR import is supported; wallet interaction requires a browser.

# Source: packages/rainbowkit/README.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/rainbowkit/README.md

# Robinhood Wallet for RainbowKit

> **AI integration docs:** [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

Add a Robinhood Wallet entry to RainbowKit with the toolkit's dedicated connection dialog.

Built and maintained by **[Vexi Lab](https://vexi-protocol.ai) (an onchain options protocol)**. This is an independent community project, **not an official Robinhood SDK**, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Robinhood.

These packages are not published to npm. Follow the [tarball installation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository) before using this adapter.

Add Robinhood first in your wallet list:

```ts
import { connectorsForWallets } from '@rainbow-me/rainbowkit';
import { injectedWallet, walletConnectWallet } from '@rainbow-me/rainbowkit/wallets';
import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-rainbowkit';

const connectors = connectorsForWallets([
  { groupName: 'Recommended', wallets: [robinhoodWallet] },
  { groupName: 'Other wallets', wallets: [injectedWallet, walletConnectWallet] },
], {
  projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID',
  appName: 'My app',
  appUrl: 'https://my-app.example',
});
```

Pass `connectors` to wagmi's `createConfig`, then use the ordinary `WagmiProvider`, `QueryClientProvider`, `RainbowKitProvider`, and `ConnectButton`. The complete runnable app is in `examples/rainbowkit`.

This adapter targets **RainbowKit 2.2.11 + wagmi 2.19.5**. RainbowKit currently declares a wagmi v2 peer; the separate wagmi adapter supports the tested v3 baseline, but that does not imply RainbowKit v3 compatibility.

Selecting Robinhood opens the SDK's native top-layer dialog, with its own close, Escape, and app-opening controls. Close it and select Robinhood again to retry. The underlying wallet chooser remains inert until the SDK dialog closes. This deliberately omits RainbowKit's `qrCode` and `mobile` hooks: RainbowKit's native Back navigation has no public cancellation callback for a pending wallet proposal. A second pairing modal or a private controller patch is unnecessary.

RainbowKit always passes a chain to wagmi's `connect`. The wagmi adapter treats it as a preference, as wagmi's built-in connectors do: if the wallet session does not approve that chain, or the in-app wallet cannot switch to it, the connection stays on the wallet's chain instead of failing. Only a user rejection of the switch fails the connection.

The adapter consumes `walletConnectParameters.metadata` generated by `connectorsForWallets`. Other generic WalletConnect provider options are not forwarded: this package owns its session transport and lifecycle. Configuration order controls the recommended group; RainbowKit may show installed or recent wallets before it according to its own settings.

For server-rendered applications, always supply an absolute HTTP(S) `appUrl` to `connectorsForWallets` as shown above. The direct `robinhoodWallet` factory also accepts `appUrl` and `appDescription`, or an explicit `walletConnectParameters.metadata` object. This lets `createConfig`, `getProvider`, and `isAuthorized` run without `window` and without requesting accounts. Browser-only applications may omit the URL to use the current origin; a factory created on the server without a URL cannot initialize a provider until a valid URL is supplied.

A displayed QR code is not proof of physical-wallet approval or network support.

# Source: packages/web3-onboard/README.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/web3-onboard/README.md

# Robinhood Wallet for Web3-Onboard

> **AI integration docs:** [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

A Robinhood Wallet module for Web3-Onboard with the toolkit's dedicated connection dialog. Web3-Onboard originated at Blocknative and is now maintained at `thirdweb-dev/web3-onboard`.

Built and maintained by **[Vexi Lab](https://vexi-protocol.ai) (an onchain options protocol)**. This is an independent community project, **not an official Robinhood SDK**, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Robinhood.

These packages are not published to npm. Follow the [tarball installation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository) before using this adapter.

```ts
import Onboard from '@web3-onboard/core';
import { robinhoodModule } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-onboard';

const onboard = Onboard({
  wallets: [robinhoodModule({ projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID' })],
  chains: [{
    id: '0x1',
    label: 'Ethereum',
    token: 'ETH',
    rpcUrl: 'https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com',
  }],
  appMetadata: { name: 'My app', description: 'My app description', explore: 'https://my-app.example' },
});

// Invoke from a user's Connect button.
const wallets = await onboard.connectWallet();
```

The module derives chain IDs and RPC URLs from Onboard's configured chains. Metadata defaults to `appMetadata`, or can be supplied explicitly to `robinhoodModule`. `getInterface` returns a stable EIP-1193 `provider` and exposes the same `RobinhoodProvider` as `instance`; it does not request accounts until Onboard calls `eth_requestAccounts`.

Robinhood's dedicated native dialog owns remote pairing cancellation. Close it and select Robinhood again to retry. A matching injected Robinhood provider is used when present. Other wallet modules remain independent. Supply a public WalletConnect project ID with the app origin allowed in its dashboard; never supply a private key or recovery phrase.

Onboard reconnects through `eth_requestAccounts`, including with `connect.autoConnectLastWallet`. The provider first recovers the session the user approved earlier, so a reload does not open a new pairing or leave the old session behind. If that session has expired or been removed, the request opens a new pairing dialog, including during an automatic reconnect. A wallet rejection is reported with code `4001`, which Onboard shows as a rejected connection with its retry action.

Compatibility baseline: `@web3-onboard/core` **2.24.1**, `@web3-onboard/common` **2.4.2**. See the standalone app in `examples/onboard` and the packed-package framework matrix.

Configuring a network does not establish wallet support for it. No transaction is sent automatically.

# Vanilla browser example

Build the packages at the repository root first with `npm ci && npm run build`.
Then run `npm install` and `npm run dev` in this directory. Copy `.env.example`
to `.env.local`, set your public WalletConnect project ID, allow the actual
example origin in your WalletConnect project, and restart the server.

`index.html` uses the real SDK and WalletConnect relay. It requests account
access only after the Connect button; it never requests a signature or transaction.

`fixture.html` uses the same SDK dialog with an explicitly synthetic transport.
Its inert QR cannot pair any wallet. It is useful for responsive presentation,
keyboard cancellation, focus restoration, and repeatable screenshots. It is
not a physical-wallet or network compatibility test.

# Source: docs/architecture.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/architecture.md

# Architecture

The SDK connects applications to Robinhood Wallet through a matching injected provider or WalletConnect. Its core provider, connection dialog, and framework adapters can be used independently of any application backend or contract deployment.

## Components

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  App[Application connect action] --> Core[RobinhoodProvider]
  Wagmi[wagmi adapter] --> Core
  RainbowKit[RainbowKit wallet entry] --> Wagmi
  Onboard[Web3-Onboard module] --> Core
  Core --> Discovery[Published Robinhood identity discovery]
  Discovery --> Injected[Matching EIP-1193 provider]
  Core --> Remote[WalletConnect SignClient transport]
  Core --> Dialog[Dedicated native HTML dialog]
  Remote --> Dialog
  Dialog --> QR[Local QR and explicit app link]
  Remote --> Session[Approved EVM session topic]
```

The core owns connection intent, timeout, cancellation, current accounts, events, and recovery. The transport owns its approved WalletConnect session topic and translates session events into EIP-1193 state. The modal owns presentation and user cancellation. Framework adapters translate public framework contracts into that common core.

`@walletconnect/sign-client` is pinned to **2.26.0**, and `qrcode` to **1.5.4**. There is no AppKit UI dependency and no private RainbowKit controller patch. Framework packages can bring their own unrelated wallet dependencies; this SDK does not assume ownership of their sessions.

## Connect lifecycle

1. Import or construct the provider without requesting accounts. `connect()` or `eth_requestAccounts` is the explicit account-permission entry point. If this connector has a persisted approval, it is recovered first, as wallets answer `eth_requestAccounts` for an existing permission; the steps below run only when recovery fails. `cancel()` also ends that recovery.
2. Discover an EIP-6963 provider advertising `com.robinhood.wallet`, or the published `isRobinhoodMobileWallet` injected flag. Identity hints are not vendor authentication.
3. Request accounts from a matching injected provider. If none is found, lazily initialize the remote transport and show the dedicated dialog when enabled.
4. Offer configured EVM chains and methods to the wallet. Render a returned, validated pairing URI as a local QR and construct the published native app route.
5. Adopt only an active attempt with valid accounts and the requested approved chain. Close its dialog, persist the session selection, and emit provider events.
6. If cancellation, expiry, failure, or a replacement attempt occurs, obsolete completion must not adopt accounts or revive the UI. Late remote approval is disconnected using its original topic.

The default error view rejects the original provider request and leaves an actionable Close view. A new user action in the host creates the retry, so wagmi and other hosts own the result of that new request. The modal's optional `onRetry` callback exists for custom hosts that deliberately own that flow; the default provider does not use it to create a hidden second request.

## Modal and nested framework UI

The dialog uses `showModal()` and the browser top layer. Its background is inert while the dialog is open, including an existing framework wallet chooser. It provides an accessible name, live status, local QR, app link, copy feedback, error details, and keyboard focus management. Escape is consumed before document-level handlers to cancel the SDK attempt while preserving the underlying chooser.

The dialog lives in an open shadow root attached to one `<rhw-connector>` element, the only node it adds to the page. Host page selectors cannot match its controls, and `:host { all: initial !important }` stops inherited host typography at the boundary. Its CSS is a constructed stylesheet where supported, so no inline `<style>` element is needed. Focus restoration follows open shadow roots, so a trigger inside another shadow tree, such as Web3-Onboard's chooser, gets focus back.

The same controls are presented as a centered dialog on wider viewports and a bottom sheet on narrow ones. Viewport width is not used to claim an app is installed. The app is opened only by an explicit anchor click.

Each modal operation carries a generation. Closing or failing clears pairing data and invalidates outstanding QR and clipboard results. A late render cannot update a reopened dialog. QR generation does not use an external image service; the wallet icon is also bundled locally. The QR canvas is drawn at the device pixel ratio (capped at 3×), and the library's fixed inline size is removed so the dialog's square, responsive CSS sizes it.

The RainbowKit adapter intentionally omits its generic `qrCode` and `mobile` display hooks. Their Back navigation has no public signal to cancel this SDK's pending proposal. Using one SDK-owned dialog gives the proposal a single, explicit cancellation boundary. RainbowKit still owns wallet grouping, installed/recent ordering, and other wallet entries.

## RPC, chain, and account boundaries

Configured chain IDs constrain the SDK's requested networks; they are not a compatibility catalog. A remote session must approve the requested chain and accounts. Only permitted wallet methods are forwarded. Supported read methods use the configured RPC endpoint for the current chain, rather than being sent to a wallet as signing requests.

`eth_accounts` returns this provider's cached accounts. `eth_chainId` returns its current hexadecimal chain value, initialized to the first configured chain before any approval. Application code must use connection status and events to distinguish that initial configuration from a confirmed wallet state.

Session events are filtered by owned topic. Account events are checked against approved accounts; removed or invalid authorization clears the connection. Event payloads are decoded as `UniversalProvider` accepts them (numeric, hexadecimal, decimal or CAIP-2 chains; plain or CAIP-10 accounts) before those checks. A session update or repeated chain event keeps the wallet-selected accounts while they remain approved, and only actual changes are emitted. A chain-switch request is checked against application configuration and session permissions, and completion must still refer to the active connection. For WalletConnect, a switch to a chain the session approved is local, because every request names its chain; a chain the session did not approve is rejected with `4901` rather than requested. No constructor, discovery call, or restore flow requests a signature or transaction.

WalletConnect `USER_REJECTED` errors (`5000`–`5003`) from a proposal or request are reported with EIP-1193 code `4001`, keeping the original error as `data`. `cancel()` ends only a pending attempt or recovery; requests on an established connection keep running.

## Persistence and teardown

The provider stores a connection marker under its stable storage prefix; the remote transport stores its owned approved-session selection. WalletConnect maintains the underlying session and cryptographic storage. Independent logical instances should use separate prefixes. Storage failure has a memory fallback for the SDK's own selection state; it holds only values that persistent storage rejected, so a removal by another tab is not masked.

WalletConnect keeps one global Core per storage prefix, and a second SignClient on that Core would add a second engine. Transports with the same prefix therefore share one SignClient for the page; a failed initialization is not cached.

`isAuthorized()` inspects previously approved state and can initialize the transport, but never calls `eth_requestAccounts`. Recovery keeps the saved chain and account selection while the session still approves them, falls back to another approved configured chain when the saved one is no longer configured, and revokes a session that approves no configured chain. A wallet's session extension refreshes the owned expiry. `disconnect()` clears local selection and disconnects the owned remote session and its pairing; revocation is best effort, because a failure (for example while offline) cannot be retried once the local pointer is cleared, so the promise still resolves. Injected-provider disconnect is local; it does not revoke the wallet's permission grant. `destroy()` removes local listeners and UI while preserving an intentionally approved persisted session for recovery by a new instance.

The `display_uri` event contains pairing material. Hosts must not log it, attach it to telemetry, or send it to third-party QR services. The SignClient is configured with silent logging and its telemetry option disabled. Those settings are not a claim that WalletConnect performs no network communication.

The implementation and tests are separate from real-device behavior, registry publication, upstream acceptance, and deployment. ## Reproduce local checks

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
npm run typecheck
npm test
node scripts/framework-matrix.mjs
```

The framework matrix writes `report.json` plus installation, build, and runtime logs into its printed temporary directory. It packs all SDK packages, computes tarball hashes, creates isolated consumer applications, installs real framework packages, type-checks/builds the examples, and runs synthetic provider lifecycle tests. Its nonempty synthetic project ID keeps connector code in the production bundle; it is not a usable relay credential.

Declared framework baselines are wagmi `2.19.5` / core `2.22.1`, wagmi `3.7.7` / core `3.6.5`, RainbowKit `2.2.11` with wagmi v2, and Web3-Onboard core `2.24.1` / common `2.4.2`. Viem is `2.57.7`. Exact resolved versions and artifacts belong in the final matrix report.

## Observed browser checks

The [browser record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/evidence/2026-10-17/browser.json) separates synthetic layout checks from actual relay initialization. Screenshots use a deliberately inert fixture QR and must never be used for wallet pairing.

### Follow-up checks

These ran after the follow-up fixes in headless Chrome for Testing 153. The synthetic fixture page was also served with an aggressive host stylesheet and with `Content-Security-Policy: style-src 'self'`. The framework pages are the packed-consumer production builds, with every request and WebSocket to a host other than `127.0.0.1` blocked. Details are in the [follow-up evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/evidence/2026-10-17/follow-up-review.json).

| Scenario | Before the fixes | After the fixes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fixture, 390×844 and 320×640 | QR displayed 240×280 (squashed); close icon off-center by (9, 7) px from the example's own `button` CSS | QR 240×240; icon centered; backing canvas 840 px at 3× |
| Fixture, 1280×720 at 2× | QR backing canvas 280 px (upscaled) | 560 px |
| Hostile host CSS | QR shrunk to 40×40, title recolored, text uppercased, close button overflowing | No host style reaches the dialog |
| `style-src 'self'` policy | Inline `<style>` blocked; dialog unstyled | No violation; fully styled |
| Keyboard | Covered by unit tests | Initial focus on Close; Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside the dialog; background inert; Close and Escape restore focus to Connect |
| RainbowKit build, network blocked | Not run | One SDK top-layer dialog over the chooser, which cannot take focus; Escape closes only the SDK dialog; RainbowKit's Retry opens a fresh one |
| Web3-Onboard build, network blocked | Not run | SDK dialog opens; Escape leads to Onboard's "Connection Rejected! Click here to try again" |
| wagmi v3 build at 390×844, network blocked | Not run | Escape returns to disconnected with focus on Connect |

On the wagmi v3 page, which loads only this SDK's connector, the only blocked host was the WalletConnect relay WebSocket. The WalletConnect telemetry and AppKit configuration hosts appeared only on the RainbowKit page, which also includes RainbowKit's own WalletConnect connector.

### Original delivery checks

The checks below were recorded on 2026-10-16 against the original delivery, before the follow-up changes, and were not repeated afterward. The real-relay rows need a project ID and should be re-run before relying on them for the current dialog.

| Scenario | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop and narrow fixture | One native top-layer dialog; local canvas QR; Robinhood name, app action, copy and help controls; no horizontal page or dialog overflow. Narrow layout uses a bottom sheet. |
| Fixture keyboard cancellation | Escape closes the dialog, returns the provider to idle and restores focus to the Connect button after its disabled state clears. Focus wrap and stale completion are also covered by modal tests. |
| Vanilla real relay | Ready QR and native Robinhood app action appeared. Cancel rejected the attempt; another Connect produced a fresh ready dialog. |
| RainbowKit real relay | Robinhood appears first in the Recommended group. Selecting it opens the SDK top-layer dialog, making the host chooser inert. Escape returns to the host chooser; its Retry action opens a fresh ready SDK dialog. Closing the chooser returns focus to Connect Wallet. |
| Web3-Onboard real relay | Selecting the module opens the ready SDK dialog. Expiry clears pairing data and shows an actionable error. Close/ Escape returns to the host rejection state; Back to wallets and the host Retry action both lead to a fresh ready SDK dialog. |
| wagmi v3 real relay | Connect opens the ready SDK dialog. Escape returns to disconnected; another Connect opens a fresh ready dialog. The final host focus refinement restores focus to Connect after cancellation and both wagmi examples passed renewed type/build checks. |

The screenshots below were recaptured after the follow-up fixes; the earlier versions, which show the squashed narrow QR and off-center close icon, remain in the repository history.

## Physical-device validation remains separate

For manual device testing, record the device model, OS, browser, Robinhood Wallet version, app origin, connector commit/tarball hash, and tested chain for each result. Use a dedicated test wallet and do not put addresses, pairing URIs, session keys, or signing material in public evidence.

1. Desktop QR to real iOS and Android wallet: scan, approve, verify account/chain result, reject, cancel, timeout, and retry. Record the error code the host receives for a wallet rejection; the SDK reports WalletConnect's `USER_REJECTED` as `4001`.
2. Same-device app handoff: explicit app-link click, successful return to the dapp, and browser behavior when the wallet is not installed. Note whether a later signing request needs a manual switch back to the wallet; the SDK does not reopen the app for requests.
3. Injected Robinhood in-app browser: discovery, user-triggered permission request, account changes, and rejected/removed authorization. With RainbowKit, confirm that connecting on a non-default configured chain shows no switch prompt.
4. Reload recovery and disconnect: recover only the intended prior approval, including through a Connect action after reload, without a new pairing; disconnect removes it; stale approval cannot revive a cancelled request.
5. Each intended network: approve it, verify actual chain selection, and exercise supported switch/rejection behavior. For WalletConnect, a switch between chains the session approved is local and shows no wallet prompt; confirm the wallet honors the next request on the selected chain. Record each mainnet and testnet separately.
6. Signing and transactions: connection checks do not require either operation. If you test them separately, use a dedicated test wallet, review every wallet prompt, and record the exact method, expected outcome and network.

Until that evidence exists, this project must not advertise physical-wallet certification or universal EVM/Robinhood Chain support.

# Source: docs/dependency-notes.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/dependency-notes.md

# Dependency audit notes

The 2026-10-17 verification used actual npm tarballs and the exact framework baselines below. Functional builds and lifecycle tests passed, but the framework consumers do not all have clean dependency audits. This is not a security audit or a production-readiness certification.

The sanitized [audit evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/evidence/2026-10-17/dependency-audit.json) records versions, package hashes, dependency paths, advisory URLs, and counts from `npm audit --json`. Counts include propagated package entries, not unique vulnerabilities or demonstrated exploits. Framework audits include their development dependencies; the standalone core install includes only its runtime dependencies.

| Consumer | Exact baseline | Moderate | High | Critical |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Standalone core | SDK 0.1.0, SignClient 2.26.0, qrcode 1.5.4 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| wagmi v3 | wagmi 3.7.7, core 3.6.5, Viem 2.57.7 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| wagmi v2 | wagmi 2.19.5, core 2.22.1, Viem 2.57.7 | 22 | 1 | 0 |
| RainbowKit | RainbowKit 2.2.11 and the wagmi v2 baseline | 24 | 1 | 0 |
| Web3-Onboard | core 2.24.1, common 2.4.2 | 4 | 5 | 3 |

## Inherited framework dependencies

The wagmi v2 and RainbowKit consumers install the broader framework connector dependency tree. Findings include `query-string 7.1.3 → decode-uri-component 0.2.2` ([decoding denial of service](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vcc3-ghjq-m6fr)), MetaMask SDK/utilities paths containing `uuid 8.3.2` and `9.0.1` ([buffer bounds](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq)), and older WalletConnect/AppKit dependencies containing `viem 2.23.2` / `isows 1.0.6 → ws 8.18.0` ([memory disclosure](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-58qx-3vcg-4xpx), [memory exhaustion](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-96hv-2xvq-fx4p)). The SDK's standalone core and the separate wagmi v3 consumer had zero reported findings in these installs.

Web3-Onboard's inherited findings include:

- `@web3-onboard/core 2.24.1 → bnc-sdk 4.6.9 → crypto-es 1.2.7`: a [critical PBKDF2 advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mpj8-q39x-wq5h). The three critical package entries include propagation through the dependency chain.
- `@web3-onboard/core 2.24.1` and `@web3-onboard/common 2.4.2 → joi 17.9.1`: [regular-expression denial of service](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6h2x-m376-mqjq), plus the additional advisory entries preserved in the evidence.
- Onboard's `viem 2.12.0 → ws 8.13.0`: [HTTP-header denial of service](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3h5v-q93c-6h6q) and the newer WebSocket advisories above.
- `@web3-onboard/core 2.24.1 → nanoid 4.0.2`: [integer overflow](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xwg4-73v4-xw9w) and additional generator advisories.
- `svelte-i18n 4.0.1 → esbuild 0.19.12`: a [development-server advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99); the example's Vite build itself uses esbuild 0.28.2.
- Onboard's `svelte 3.59.2`: [DOM-clobbering XSS](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rcqx-6q8c-2c42) and additional SSR/escaping advisory entries.

No force-fix, dependency override, or unsupported major framework upgrade was applied. In particular, RainbowKit 2.2.11 declares wagmi v2 support; substituting wagmi v3 would invalidate the tested integration baseline. Consumers need their own dependency and deployment review.

## Onboard bundle and option check

The tested Onboard public API has no `connect.disableUD` analytics switch. Its deprecated `connect.disableUDResolution` option concerns optional Unstoppable Domains resolution; the [source declaration](https://github.com/thirdweb-dev/web3-onboard/blob/03b25b0ade48b7cc8d48dd408741c7e211cf22ac/packages/core/src/types.ts#L275) does not describe telemetry control.

The inspected Onboard source uses `bnc-sdk` in type-only imports. A production build of this exact example with source maps enabled produced 18 maps and 803 source entries; none identified `bnc-sdk` or `crypto-es`. That is a limited observation about this example's generated bundle. It neither removes the installed dependency findings nor proves that another consumer cannot reach affected code, and no configuration option is presented as a security mitigation.

# Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing

This repository contains the provider, connection UI, framework adapters, examples and tests. You can develop it from a single checkout.

For integration help, start with [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) and the [AI integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md).

## Set up a checkout

Use Node.js 22.12 or newer and npm. CI runs the build, type check and unit tests on Node.js 22.12.0 and 24, and the packed framework matrix on 24.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector.git
cd robinhood-wallet-connector
npm ci
npm run build
npm run typecheck
npm test
```

The packages are currently unpublished. For installation in another application, follow the [tarball installation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository).

## Repository layout

| Directory | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/core` | EIP-1193 provider, discovery, WalletConnect transport and connection dialog |
| `packages/wagmi` | wagmi v2/v3 connector |
| `packages/rainbowkit` | RainbowKit wallet entry |
| `packages/web3-onboard` | Web3-Onboard wallet module |
| `examples` | Vanilla, wagmi v2/v3, RainbowKit and Onboard applications |
| `tests` | Synthetic provider, transport, modal and framework consumer checks |
| `scripts/framework-matrix.mjs` | Packed-package compatibility checks |
| `docs` | Architecture, verification records, dependency notes and upstream contribution guidance |
| `llms.txt` | Curated documentation index for AI agents |
| `llms-full.txt` | Generated full-text integration documentation |
| `scripts/llms-docs.mjs` | Documentation bundle generation, freshness and link checks |

Rebuild the packages after changing their source; examples consume their generated exports.

## Run an example

After the root build, enter the example directory and follow its README. For example:

```sh
cd examples/wagmi-v3
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local
# Set VITE_WC_PROJECT_ID in .env.local to your WalletConnect project ID.
npm run dev
```

Allow the example's actual origin in your WalletConnect project settings, then restart the dev server after changing environment variables. The project ID is a public application identifier. Never enter a recovery phrase or private key.

The vanilla example also provides `fixture.html`, which uses a synthetic transport for layout and keyboard checks without a live project ID. Its QR cannot pair a wallet. See the [vanilla example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/vanilla/README.md) for details.

## Validate a change

For provider or adapter changes, run the root build, type check and unit tests above. The type check also covers the test files. Test the affected integrations against packed packages:

```sh
node scripts/framework-matrix.mjs
# Or select one or more cases:
node scripts/framework-matrix.mjs wagmi-v2 wagmi-v3
```

Available cases are `wagmi-v2`, `wagmi-v3`, `rainbowkit` and `onboard`. The script downloads real npm framework dependencies into separate temporary applications, builds them, and runs synthetic lifecycle tests. It prints the location of `report.json` and the install/build/test logs. These checks do not need a live WalletConnect project ID or an approved wallet.

Add regression coverage when changing connection behavior, particularly cancellation, late results, session recovery, account/chain events and teardown. Browser presentation changes also need desktop and narrow-viewport checks. Use the [verification guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md) to record what was actually tested; a rendered QR does not prove successful mobile pairing.

For documentation-only changes, check links, examples, JSON records and whitespace. A full wallet test run is unnecessary when executable code and package configuration are unchanged.

## Maintain the AI documentation

Documentation is part of the change. Whenever public APIs, options, connection behavior, installation, package versions, supported frameworks, publication status or verification claims change, update the affected guides in the same PR and review `llms.txt` and `docs/ai-integration.md`. If their content remains accurate, explain that in the PR checklist.

`llms.txt` is a short, curated map with direct text links. `llms-full.txt` is generated from the canonical guides listed in `scripts/llms-docs.mjs`; edit those guides instead of the generated file. Include new or moved documentation in the index and bundle source list when relevant, then run:

```sh
npm run docs:generate
npm run docs:check
```

Commit the resulting `llms-full.txt` update with its source changes. The documentation commands use Node.js built-ins and do not require installing wallet dependencies. CI rejects stale generated content and broken local or same-repository documentation links. It does not establish that external websites are reachable or that an API description matches runtime behavior; review those separately.

Keep the README's agent entry points prominent and package keywords and GitHub About accurate. Publishing an index improves navigation; it does not guarantee search ranking or automatic adoption by an AI service.

## Submit a pull request

Create a focused branch and describe the problem, resulting behavior and checks you ran. Keep code, comments and public text in English. Update the relevant API documentation and examples when their behavior changes. Discuss substantial API or dependency changes in a repository issue before implementing them.

Keep credentials and wallet pairing material out of commits, logs and screenshots. Preserve third-party license and asset attribution. Consult the [dependency notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/dependency-notes.md) before changing framework versions, and the [upstream contribution guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/upstream-contributions.md) when proposing an integration to another project.

# Source: AGENTS.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/AGENTS.md

# Guidance for coding assistants

This is a standalone SDK repository. Start with [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) for the documentation map and [the integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md) for using the SDK. Read [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md) for installation and public APIs, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for setup, repository layout, checks and pull requests. All development instructions are maintained in this repository.

- Use English for code, comments, documentation and interface text.
- Keep changes focused and preserve unrelated working-tree changes. Do not bypass hooks or force-push.
- Keep imports safe without a browser. Initialize transport only when needed; request accounts only after explicit connection intent.
- Identify Robinhood providers using the documented discovery metadata. Never relabel an arbitrary injected provider.
- Cover cancellation, late completion, retry, disconnect, restored sessions and event cleanup when changing those behaviors.
- Validate compatibility using the real framework packages and packed consumers. Do not claim support for untested versions or networks.
- Use synthetic wallets for automated checks. Do not approve real wallet prompts, request signatures or send transactions during automated UI tests.
- Keep pairing URIs, session keys, account information and authentication material out of logs, screenshots and committed artifacts.
- Preserve the distinction between synthetic tests, browser checks and physical-device results when updating verification records.
- Do not imply Robinhood endorsement. Keep third-party asset attribution and license notices intact.

## Keep agent documentation current

- In the same pull request as changes to public exports, options, connection behavior, installation, package versions, supported frameworks, publication status or verification claims, update the affected canonical guides and review `llms.txt` and `docs/ai-integration.md`. Update their summaries and links whenever the change affects them; explain any not-applicable decision in the PR.
- Keep the `llms.txt` entry visible near the top of the root and package READMEs. Its links must lead to existing public documentation; use raw text URLs for files that agents should fetch directly.
- Treat `llms-full.txt` as generated output. After editing included documentation, run `npm run docs:generate`, commit the generated update, and run `npm run docs:check` before committing. Do not hand-edit the generated file. CI checks freshness and documentation links.
- When adding or moving a guide or example, update `llms.txt` and the source list in `scripts/llms-docs.mjs` if the document belongs in the full-text bundle.
- Keep GitHub About/topics and package metadata consistent with implemented support. Describe proposed integrations as proposals; never advertise planned adapters as available or unpublished packages as registry releases.
